tasks.name: Fiction · commitment
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Continue the scene. Mara promised Ivo to return his compass before dawn. The bridge is flooded. The ferryman will cross only if she helps secure his leaking boat, which may take until sunrise. Keep the characters and constraints consistent.

tasks.name: Fiction · changed evidence
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Continue the scene. Engineer Lena blames a faulty sensor for a heat warning. A second independent sensor now reports the same rise. Her manager wants the test completed tonight. Show what happens next through actions and dialogue.

tasks.name: Dialogue · disagreement
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Write a dialogue between Nia and Omar. Nia wants to publish their experiment tonight; Omar found that the main effect disappears in a control condition. Neither is malicious. They must decide what to tell their team.

tasks.name: News · uncertainty
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Write a short news report using only these facts: the city’s river gauge rose 12 cm overnight; two roads were closed as a precaution; the weather office expects more rain but cannot yet predict the peak; no injuries have been reported. Distinguish fact from forecast.

tasks.name: Explanation · misleading correlation
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Explain why ice cream sales and river rescues might rise together even if buying ice cream does not cause accidents. Give a concrete alternative cause, what data would help distinguish it, and one limitation of that test.

tasks.name: Planning · competing constraints
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Plan a small community exhibition. There are 200 credits, two volunteers, one afternoon, no internet, and visitors with different reading abilities. The exhibition must explain a local water-quality result honestly. Give priorities and a fallback if a volunteer cannot come.

tasks.name: Advice · interpersonal repair
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Write a message to a friend whose borrowed book you accidentally damaged. The book had handwritten notes that cannot be replaced. You can afford a new copy but cannot undo the lost notes. Avoid treating payment as a complete solution.

tasks.name: Argument · competing values
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. A town must choose between a quiet riverside habitat and a well-used cycling route. Explain a reasonable case on each side, propose a compromise, and say what evidence could show that your compromise fails.

tasks.name: Perspective · different knowledge
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Tell a brief scene: Ava leaves a key in a drawer, exits, and does not see Ben move it into a box. Ben assumes she watched. Ava returns to fetch it. Develop the resulting misunderstanding without making either character know something they did not observe.

tasks.name: Speculation · consistent world
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Describe a morning in a city where people can lend each other ten minutes of remembered skill, but the lender temporarily loses that skill. Develop a concrete consequence through one character’s small decision. Keep the rule consistent.

tasks.name: Summary · preserving limitations
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Summarize for a colleague: A school tested a reading app in two classes. Scores rose in both, more in the app class. The classes had different teachers and were not randomly assigned. Some students stopped using the app. The school wants to know whether it should buy a licence. Preserve what is and is not supported.

tasks.name: Editing · evidence-sensitive revision
tasks.text: Give only the requested response, about 80–100 words. Rewrite this public claim accurately, then explain the most important change: ‘Our device proved that the new filter makes all drinking water safe. We tested six samples from one tap and all passed the bacterial test. Therefore no other checks are needed.’

concepts.name: Sentence completion
concepts.definition: Sentences reach a grammatically complete ending.

concepts.name: Grammatical agreement
concepts.definition: Verb tense, number and pronouns agree.

concepts.name: Tense consistency
concepts.definition: Tense remains appropriate and consistent across the response.

concepts.name: Clear references
concepts.definition: It is clear who pronouns and referring expressions denote.

concepts.name: Precise word choice
concepts.definition: Words convey specific actions or relations rather than vague placeholders.

concepts.name: Vocabulary variety
concepts.definition: The response varies word choice without merely substituting synonyms.

concepts.name: Sentence structure variety
concepts.definition: Sentence constructions vary in a purposeful way.

concepts.name: Nested reasoning in sentences
concepts.definition: Sentences express multiple related clauses accurately.

concepts.name: Concision
concepts.definition: The response conveys relevant content without unnecessary repetition.

concepts.name: Connections between sentences
concepts.definition: Sentences connect by clear references and transitions.

concepts.name: Overall organization
concepts.definition: Parts appear in an order that helps the requested task.

concepts.name: Readable prose
concepts.definition: The response can be followed without decoding awkward phrasing.

concepts.name: Formal register
concepts.definition: The language uses a formal professional or academic register.

concepts.name: Conversational register
concepts.definition: The language resembles natural informal conversation.

concepts.name: Figurative language
concepts.definition: Metaphor or comparison adds a nonliteral way of describing the situation.

concepts.name: Sensory detail
concepts.definition: Concrete sights, sounds or physical sensations are described.

concepts.name: Concrete detail
concepts.definition: Specific objects, actions, places or quantities develop the answer.

concepts.name: Direct speech
concepts.definition: Quoted speech or an actual exchange between speakers appears.

concepts.name: Variation in pacing
concepts.definition: Sentence lengths and paragraph pacing vary with the content.

concepts.name: Repeated structure
concepts.definition: The same sentence or rhetorical pattern is used repeatedly.

concepts.name: Causal development
concepts.definition: Events or claims follow through causes rather than merely occurring in sequence.

concepts.name: Goal continuity
concepts.definition: An established goal remains relevant as the response develops.

concepts.name: Constraint tracking
concepts.definition: The response respects stated practical constraints.

concepts.name: Character continuity
concepts.definition: Characters retain established information, motives and relationships.

concepts.name: Character agency
concepts.definition: Characters make consequential choices rather than only reacting passively.

concepts.name: Change in a character
concepts.definition: The response develops a change in a character’s outlook or conduct.

concepts.name: Multiple viewpoints
concepts.definition: Different perspectives are represented distinctly.

concepts.name: Different beliefs
concepts.definition: The response distinguishes what different people believe or know.

concepts.name: Development of conflict
concepts.definition: A tension or obstacle is developed rather than instantly erased.

concepts.name: Resolution
concepts.definition: The response brings its central task or conflict to a meaningful stopping point.

concepts.name: Open ending
concepts.definition: The response deliberately leaves a consequential question unresolved.

concepts.name: Unexpected development
concepts.definition: A development departs from the most straightforward continuation while staying coherent.

concepts.name: Imaginative alternatives
concepts.definition: The response invents a plausible new possibility beyond the supplied setup.

concepts.name: Consistent imagined world
concepts.definition: Invented details remain compatible with the situation.

concepts.name: Development of a theme
concepts.definition: A broader concern such as trust or responsibility recurs through concrete events.

concepts.name: Explicit moral lesson
concepts.definition: The response explicitly tells the reader a lesson or moral.

concepts.name: Positive tone
concepts.definition: The response expresses hope, warmth or a favorable outlook.

concepts.name: Negative tone
concepts.definition: The response expresses loss, hostility or an unfavorable outlook.

concepts.name: Emotional intensity
concepts.definition: Emotion is strongly expressed in actions or language.

concepts.name: Emotional nuance
concepts.definition: Emotions are mixed, qualified or develop rather than being only named.

concepts.name: Attention to another’s feelings
concepts.definition: The response acknowledges another person’s emotional perspective.

concepts.name: Anxiety or apprehension
concepts.definition: Concern about uncertain danger shapes the response.

concepts.name: Anger or blame
concepts.definition: Anger, accusation or blame is expressed.

concepts.name: Sadness or grief
concepts.definition: Sadness, disappointment or grief shapes the response.

concepts.name: Wonder or curiosity
concepts.definition: The response explores surprise or interest in possibilities.

concepts.name: Humor
concepts.definition: The response attempts a playful or comic effect.

concepts.name: Emotional restraint
concepts.definition: The response handles charged material without overt emotional display.

concepts.name: Change of emotional tone
concepts.definition: The emotional tone changes meaningfully during the response.

concepts.name: Cooperative approach
concepts.definition: The response seeks a joint solution or shared understanding.

concepts.name: Assertive approach
concepts.definition: The response clearly states or defends a position or boundary.

concepts.name: Deference
concepts.definition: The response yields judgment or authority to another person.

concepts.name: Confrontation
concepts.definition: The response directly challenges another’s conduct or claim.

concepts.name: Trust
concepts.definition: The response treats another person as reliable or acts on that assumption.

concepts.name: Suspicion
concepts.definition: The response questions another person’s motives or reliability.

concepts.name: Care for welfare
concepts.definition: The response acts to protect or improve someone’s welfare.

concepts.name: Fairness
concepts.definition: The response considers balanced treatment or others’ legitimate interests.

concepts.name: Persuasion
concepts.definition: The response tries to change a person’s belief or choice with reasons.

concepts.name: Acknowledgment of fault
concepts.definition: The response accepts responsibility or apologizes for a specific fault.

concepts.name: Repair of a relationship
concepts.definition: The response takes a concrete step to repair trust or understanding.

concepts.name: Boundary setting
concepts.definition: The response states limits on conduct or obligations.

concepts.name: Use of supplied evidence
concepts.definition: Claims are linked to evidence in the task.

concepts.name: Revision after contrary evidence
concepts.definition: The response revises or qualifies a belief when contrary evidence appears.

concepts.name: Explicit uncertainty
concepts.definition: The response distinguishes what is known from what remains uncertain.

concepts.name: Alternative explanations
concepts.definition: More than one plausible explanation or course is considered.

concepts.name: Counterfactual reasoning
concepts.definition: The response explains what would change under a different condition.

concepts.name: Caution about causation
concepts.definition: The response avoids treating a coincidence as proof of a cause.

concepts.name: Stepwise planning
concepts.definition: The response organizes actions to achieve a goal.

concepts.name: Sensitivity to risk
concepts.definition: The response notices and acts on possible harmful consequences.

concepts.name: Long-term consequences
concepts.definition: The response considers consequences beyond the immediate next action.

concepts.name: Correction within the response
concepts.definition: The response identifies and corrects its own stated error or premature conclusion.

concepts.name: Justification
concepts.definition: Important recommendations or conclusions are accompanied by reasons.

concepts.name: Abstraction from examples
concepts.definition: The response extracts a useful general relation rather than only listing details.

concepts.name: Following the requested task
concepts.definition: The response actually performs the requested task and format.

concepts.name: Consistency with supplied facts
concepts.definition: The response does not contradict facts given in the prompt.

concepts.name: Unsupported factual invention
concepts.definition: The response adds factual claims not supported by the supplied information; invention is allowed in explicitly fictional tasks.

concepts.name: Relevance
concepts.definition: The response stays focused on what was asked.

concepts.name: Practical usefulness
concepts.definition: The response gives content a reader could use for the requested purpose.

concepts.name: Coverage of the task
concepts.definition: The response covers the task’s important requested parts.

concepts.name: Visible breakdown
concepts.definition: The response has incoherence, empty looping or unrelated fragments.

concepts.name: Adaptation to genre
concepts.definition: The response adopts an appropriate form for news, dialogue, fiction, explanation or planning as requested.
